tips.brand: FetlinePounce by Studio 87, a fast limiting amplifier.
tips.pName: Open the preset browser. Double-click to rename your own preset.
tips.pSave: Save these settings as your own preset. Asks before overwriting.
tips.bBypass: Bypass: hear the dry signal to compare with the processed sound (B). The meters keep moving.
tips.bSettings: Info bubbles, power saving, colour look, window size.
tips.bAbout: About FetlinePounce, support and where your files live.
tips.vu: The needle meter. It shows gain reduction in dB, or the output level, depending on the Meter switch below. The scale is in dB.
tips.cvCurve: Level in (across) against level out (up), in dB. The dashed line marks the fixed threshold: turning Input up moves it to the left, so the signal pushes further into it. The dot is the live signal.
tips.cvHist: How much the limiter turned the signal down, in dB, over the last six seconds.
tips.cvTime: Left: how fast the gain comes down after a loud hit, in milliseconds. Right: how it lets go, in milliseconds. Solid: after a short hit. Dashed: after a long loud passage, when release is slower.
tips.cvIn: Input level in dB (peak). Click to clear the clip light.
tips.cvOut: Output level in dB (peak). Blue is safe, purple is loud, pink is clipping. Click to clear the clip light.
tips.kHP: Listen HP: the level detector ignores everything below about 100 Hz, so the bass does not trigger the limiter so hard. The sound itself is not filtered.
tips.cheek: Double-click the wood to reset the window to 100%.
tips.mixKnob: Blend of the dry signal and the limited signal, for parallel compression. 100% is all limited. Double-click to reset.

kcells.labTip: How hard the sound is pushed into the limiter. More Input means more squashing and more colour. Try: turn it up until the needle moves 3 to 6 dB on the loud parts, then lift Output to match the level.
kcells.knobTip: How hard the sound is pushed into the limiter. More Input means more squashing and more colour. Try: turn it up until the needle moves 3 to 6 dB on the loud parts, then lift Output to match the level.

kcells.labTip: The final volume after the limiter. It does not change how much limiting happens. Try: raise it to make up the level lost by squashing, and use Bypass (B) to check it is not just louder.
kcells.knobTip: The final volume after the limiter. It does not change how much limiting happens. Try: raise it to make up the level lost by squashing, and use Bypass (B) to check it is not just louder.

kcells.labTip: How fast the limiter reacts to a loud sound. Clockwise is faster. Try: fast attack grabs the punch of drums and tames peaks; slow attack lets the front of each hit through, so drums keep their snap.
kcells.knobTip: How fast the limiter reacts to a loud sound. Clockwise is faster. Try: fast attack grabs the punch of drums and tames peaks; slow attack lets the front of each hit through, so drums keep their snap.

kcells.labTip: How fast the limiter lets go after a loud sound. Clockwise is faster. Try: fast release pumps and sounds lively; slow release is smoother and calmer. It adapts a little: quicker after short hits, slower after long loud parts.
kcells.knobTip: How fast the limiter lets go after a loud sound. Clockwise is faster. Try: fast release pumps and sounds lively; slow release is smoother and calmer. It adapts a little: quicker after short hits, slower after long loud parts.

keys.tip: 4 to 1: the gentlest. It evens out a sound. Try it first on vocals and mixes.
8 to 1: firmer. Try it on drums and bass.
12 to 1: strong, close to limiting. Try it on loud, spiky sounds.
20 to 1: limiting. It stops peaks hard. Try it to catch the loudest hits.
Every ratio button at once: a harsh, loud, squashed sound with a lot of distortion. Try it on drum rooms or for effect. Click again to go back.
The needle shows how many dB the limiter turns the sound down. Try it while setting Input: 3 to 6 dB is a good start.
The needle shows the output level, with 0 at a loud reference. Try it to check your level after Output.
The needle shows the output level, with 0 at a quieter reference. Try it for gentler material.
The needle is switched off. The sound does not change. Try it to judge by ear only.
Listen HP: the level detector ignores everything below about 100 Hz, so the bass does not trigger the limiter so hard. The sound itself is not filtered.
